cards.headline: S[10kKO] is right: once White connects, each side must fill a shared liberty before its ko capture threatens to win. The checker followed a White mistake.

diagrams.caption: The tree's line to the leaf, marked S[10kKO]. White to play; Black can take the ko by capturing White 6.

diagrams.moves: D16 A19 pass C17 A18 A19! pass A16
diagrams.caption: White 12 connects, Black 13 takes the ko and White 14 waits. Black 15 invests, White 16 retakes for free and threatens to capture at A16, so Black needs a threat for Black 17 before Black 19 captures.

The checker's line: White 12 fills a shared liberty itself, and Black 13 takes the ko. Both captures now threaten at once and Black took first, a direct ko Black wins with equal threats: one threat better for Black than Diagram 2.

text: After White 12 in Diagram 2 joins White's groups, A16 and C17 are liberties of both White's group and Black's three inner stones. Whoever fills one hands the other side a free ko capture that threatens to win at once. That is your 10kKO, and Black needs one threat more, a count decided in the narrow area.

The checker's KO? came from the line in Diagram 3, where White fills A16 itself: a mistake that costs White a threat. It read that line because it left the count undecided. Question 1a does not change the verdict: 10kKO is either exact here or ranks equal to A-1KO+, and the checker's KO? is wrong under either answer.

cards.headline: White has just retaken the ko, and Black's retake still needs one approach: S[A-1KO-], not S[A-1KO+].

diagrams.caption: The tree's line to the leaf, marked S[A-1KO+]. White 16 has just retaken the ko. Black to play.

diagrams.moves: A19! pass A14 A18 A19! pass A16
diagrams.caption: Black 17 retakes with a threat, and after White 18 plays elsewhere Black 19 approaches. White 20 retakes for free, so Black needs a second threat for Black 21 before Black 23 captures.

diagrams.moves: A19! F18 G19 A18 A19! pass A14 A18 A19! pass A16
diagrams.caption: White 18 ataris Black 15 before the approach, Black 19 answers, and White 20 retakes for free. Black needs a threat for each of Black 17, Black 21 and Black 25.

text: White 16 has just retaken the ko, and Black's four stones are in atari at A16, so White's capture threatens at once. Black must retake with a threat, and its retake threatens nothing until Black 19 in Diagram 2 fills A14; then White 20 retakes for free. One approach with White taking first is A-1KO-, a count of two. The tree's A-1KO+ says one, and looks carried over from Black 13's take.

White can gain one more threat before the approach (Diagram 3), so Black in fact needs three; that count is decided in the narrow area only. It is your c121 pattern: what White gains with its free move in an approach round belongs to the approach, so the label stays A-1KO-, and the strict label is A-1KO-2. Answer White 18 at G19, as Black 19 does in Diagram 3: on the open board, F17 would leave White a second atari.

cards.headline: White took first and Black needs one approach, not two: S[A-1KO-], not S[A-2KO+]. After Black retakes, White must extend; connecting dies.

diagrams.caption: The tree's line to the leaf, marked S[A-2KO+]. White 12 has just taken the ko. Black to play.

diagrams.moves: A19! E19 F19 A18 A19! pass C19 pass C17
diagrams.caption: Black 13 retakes with a threat and ataris White 2. White 14 extends, Black 15 approaches, and White 16 retakes for free. With a second threat Black 17 retakes, and Black 19 and Black 21 capture.
If White 14 connects instead, Black 15 throws in, White 16 takes five stones, and Black 17 takes the vital point of the bulky five. White dies without a ko.
The checker's approach: if White 14 plays elsewhere, Black 15 captures White 2 and starts a second ko. White has no free retake: A18 would be suicide, and B19 would retake a ko.

text: White 12 has just taken the ko, and Black's three stones are in atari at C17, so White's capture threatens at once. In Diagram 2 Black needs exactly one approach, Black 15, before its retake threatens to win at once, and White 16 then retakes for free. That is S[A-1KO-], two threats more than White. The tree's A-2KO+ has the same count, but no line gives Black two approaches, and Black did not take first. besogo ranks A-1KO- above A-2KO+ for Black, so this is no notation difference.

White must extend, as White 14 does in Diagram 2; connecting dies to the throw-in in Diagram 3. The checker's A-1KO+ took Black 15 in Diagram 4 as the approach, but that capture starts a second ko and leaves White no free retake, and White's extension prevents it at no cost.

In the wider search area the count stays partly undecided; only gains in the approach round could raise it, and your c121 rule keeps those out of the label. A fully open board was not tested (question 8); there, a White atari on Black 15 in Diagram 2 might become a real threat.

cards.headline: White 14 is the first ko capture and threatens at once, and Black's retake needs one approach: S[A-1KO-], two threats more, not S[A-1KO+].

diagrams.caption: The tree's line to the leaf, marked S[A-1KO+]. White 14 has just taken the ko. Black to play.

diagrams.moves: A16! pass A14 A17 A16! pass A19
diagrams.caption: Black 15 retakes with a threat, and after White 16 plays elsewhere Black 17 approaches. White 18 retakes for free, so Black needs a second threat for Black 19 before Black 21 captures.

text: White 14 is the first ko capture: Black 9 captured White 6 but kept two liberties, so it was no ko capture. Black's four stones are in atari at A19, so White's capture threatens at once. Black must retake with a threat, and its retake threatens nothing until Black 17 in Diagram 2 fills A14; then White 18 retakes for free. One approach with White taking first is A-1KO-: Black needs two threats more than White. The tree's A-1KO+ says one, and Black fails with one.

Not settled here: the tree's other S[A-1KO+] leaf on this ko is the same position without Black 11 and White 12, and in the narrow area Black fails there even with three threats more. A grading check should look at it together with this leaf.
